```{r setup, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
# the code of the benchmark is in two scripts in the directory code (one to
# simulate the tracks, one to run the benchmark), from which the chunks below
# are read (purl = FALSE because pkgdown purls this file from the package
# root when looking for images, where these relative paths do not exist)
knitr::read_chunk("code/operations_benchmark_tracks.R")
knitr::read_chunk("code/operations_benchmark.R")
```

`tidytracks` works on `move2` objects, and many of its functions do what
other packages for tracking data also do. This article compares how long
`tidytracks` takes for three common operations with other packages that
offer them:

- the distance between consecutive locations of each track (step lengths),
  with `move2` (Kranstauber et al. 2024), `amt` (Signer et al. 2019) and
  `trip` (Sumner 2011);
- the speed filter of McConnell et al. (1992), with `trip`, from which
  `tidytracks` ported it;
- splitting the tracks of a central place forager into trips away from its
  nest, with `track2KBA` (Beal et al. 2021).

It also checks that, given the same settings, they give the same results,
and shows how the time of each operation grows with the size of the data, up
to tens of millions of locations.

The [results](#results) come first. The second part,
[How the benchmark was run](#how-the-benchmark-was-run), describes the
simulated tracks and the benchmark, with their code, and how to run it again.

# Results

```{r results_packages, include = FALSE}
# to summarise and plot the results
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r read_results, include = FALSE}
# the results of the benchmark, saved by the script in the directory data
timings <- read.csv("data/operations_benchmark_timings.csv")
checks <- read.csv("data/operations_benchmark_checks.csv")
session <- read.csv("data/operations_benchmark_session.csv")
```

```{r check_numbers, include = FALSE}
# the value of a check, summed over the two data sets
check_total <- function(operation, package, check) {
  sum(checks$value[
    checks$operation == operation & checks$package == package &
      checks$check == check
  ])
}
# a count, with a comma for thousands, for the text and tables, or "none"
count <- function(operation, package, check, zero = "0") {
  n <- check_total(operation, package, check)
  if (n == 0) zero else format(n, big.mark = ",")
}
# a count with its noun, e.g. "no trips", "1 trip" or "1,000 trips"
count_of <- function(operation, package, check, noun) {
  n <- check_total(operation, package, check)
  paste(
    count(operation, package, check, zero = "no"),
    if (n == 1) noun else paste0(noun, "s")
  )
}
# the largest relative difference between step distances (in %), over the
# two data sets
distance_diff <- function(package) {
  100 * max(checks$value[
    checks$operation == "distance" & checks$package == package
  ])
}
# the text below assumes that the distances of trip and tidytracks are the
# same (up to rounding errors), that all the tracks in which tidytracks and
# trip flag different locations have an outlier as their second-to-last
# location, and that tidytracks and track2KBA put the same locations in
# trips, except at the ends of trips and tracks
stopifnot(
  distance_diff("trip") < 1e-7,
  check_total(
    "speed_filter", "trip", "tracks with locations flagged differently"
  ) ==
    check_total(
      "speed_filter", "trip",
      "tracks with an outlier second to last, flagged differently"
    ),
  check_total(
    "trip_split", "both", "other locations in a trip in only one package"
  ) == 0
)
trip_version <- session$value[session$item == "trip"]
```

```{r read_timings, include = FALSE}
operation_labels <- c(
  distance = "Step distances",
  speed_filter = "Speed filter",
  trip_split = "Trip split"
)
dataset_labels <- c(
  medium = "Medium tracks",
  long = "Long tracks",
  season = "Tracks of a season",
  year = "Tracks of a year"
)
# the data sets on which the times grow (copies of the medium and long
# tracks), and those on which the packages are compared (copies of the tracks
# of a season and of a year)
growth_sets <- c("medium", "long")
compared_sets <- c("season", "year")
package_levels <- c("tidytracks", "move2", "amt", "trip", "track2KBA")
timings <- timings %>%
  mutate(
    total = tracks * locations,
    data_set = paste(
      format(tracks, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), "tracks of",
      format(locations, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), "locations"
    ),
    operation = factor(operation_labels[operation], operation_labels),
    dataset = factor(dataset_labels[dataset], dataset_labels),
    package = factor(package, package_levels)
  )
# the packages compared for each operation
operation_packages <- distinct(timings, operation, package)
# the packages are compared on the copies of the tracks of a season and of a
# year, with the operations that were not run on them
compared <- timings %>%
  filter(dataset %in% dataset_labels[compared_sets]) %>%
  mutate(data_set = factor(data_set, unique(data_set)))
not_run <- compared %>%
  distinct(dataset, data_set) %>%
  cross_join(operation_packages) %>%
  anti_join(compared, by = c("dataset", "operation", "package"))
# the times on the copies of the medium and long tracks, up to the most copies
growth_timings <- timings %>%
  filter(dataset %in% dataset_labels[growth_sets]) %>%
  mutate(dataset = droplevels(dataset))
most_copies <- max(growth_timings$copies)
```

```{r timing_numbers, include = FALSE}
# the most copies of a data set
copies_of <- function(dataset) {
  max(timings$copies[timings$dataset == dataset_labels[[dataset]]])
}
# the time (s) of an operation with a package, on copies of a data set (by
# default the most copies)
time_of <- function(operation, package, dataset, copies = NULL) {
  if (is.null(copies)) {
    copies <- copies_of(dataset)
  }
  timings$seconds[
    timings$operation == operation_labels[[operation]] &
      timings$package == package &
      timings$dataset == dataset_labels[[dataset]] &
      timings$copies == copies
  ]
}
# a number with 2 significant digits, for the text
fmt <- function(x) {
  trimws(formatC(signif(x, 2), format = "fg", digits = 2, big.mark = ","))
}
# a time, in seconds, or in minutes from a minute, or in hours from an hour
fmt_time <- function(seconds) {
  case_when(
    seconds < 60 ~ paste(fmt(seconds), "s"),
    seconds < 3600 ~ paste(fmt(seconds / 60), "min"),
    TRUE ~ paste(fmt(seconds / 3600), "h")
  )
}
secs <- function(operation, package, dataset, copies = NULL) {
  fmt_time(time_of(operation, package, dataset, copies))
}
# the time relative to tidytracks
ratio <- function(operation, package, dataset, copies = NULL) {
  time_of(operation, package, dataset, copies) /
    time_of(operation, "tidytracks", dataset, copies)
}
# the ratios on two data sets (by default those on which the packages are
# compared), e.g. "2 to 3", or "2" if they are the same
ratio_range <- function(operation, package, datasets = compared_sets,
                        copies = NULL) {
  ratios <- fmt(range(vapply(
    datasets,
    function(dataset) ratio(operation, package, dataset, copies),
    numeric(1)
  )))
  if (ratios[1] == ratios[2]) {
    ratios[1]
  } else {
    paste(ratios[1], "to", ratios[2])
  }
}
# the times on the data sets on which the packages are compared, e.g. "12 s
# and 13 s", or "13 s" if they are the same
time_range <- function(operation, package, datasets = compared_sets) {
  times <- vapply(
    datasets,
    function(dataset) secs(operation, package, dataset),
    character(1)
  )
  paste(unique(times), collapse = " and ")
}
# the number of tracks and of locations of copies of a data set (by default
# the most copies)
size_of <- function(dataset, copies = NULL, what = "tracks") {
  if (is.null(copies)) {
    copies <- copies_of(dataset)
  }
  format(
    unique(timings[[what]][
      timings$dataset == dataset_labels[[dataset]] & timings$copies == copies
    ]),
    big.mark = ","
  )
}
# the most copies on which track2KBA was run, and their number of locations
kba_copies <- max(timings$copies[timings$package == "track2KBA"])
kba_locations <- unique(
  timings$total[timings$package == "track2KBA" & timings$copies == kba_copies]
)
```

```{r growth_numbers, include = FALSE}
# the medium and long tracks have the same number of locations, for the same
# number of copies
stopifnot(all(
  timings$total[timings$dataset == dataset_labels[["medium"]]] ==
    timings$total[timings$dataset == dataset_labels[["long"]]]
))
all_copies <- sort(unique(timings$copies))
most_locations <- max(timings$total)
# the time per location (in microseconds) on the most copies of a data set
per_location <- function(operation, package, dataset) {
  fmt(1e6 * time_of(operation, package, dataset) / most_locations)
}
# the overhead of each track (in ms), from the times on the same number of
# locations in the medium and long tracks
per_track_ms <- function(operation, package, copies = most_copies) {
  n_tracks <- function(dataset) {
    unique(timings$tracks[
      timings$dataset == dataset_labels[[dataset]] & timings$copies == copies
    ])
  }
  time_diff <- time_of(operation, package, "medium", copies) -
    time_of(operation, package, "long", copies)
  1000 * time_diff / (n_tracks("medium") - n_tracks("long"))
}
per_track <- function(operation, package, copies = most_copies) {
  fmt(per_track_ms(operation, package, copies))
}
# how many times longer an operation takes on 10 times as many copies
growth_ratio <- function(operation, package, dataset, copies) {
  time_of(operation, package, dataset, 10 * copies) /
    time_of(operation, package, dataset, copies)
}
growth <- function(operation, package, dataset, copies) {
  fmt(growth_ratio(operation, package, dataset, copies))
}
# how many times as many medium tracks as long tracks
track_ratio <- unique(
  timings$tracks[timings$dataset == dataset_labels[["medium"]]] /
    timings$tracks[timings$dataset == dataset_labels[["long"]]]
)
# the time (s) that track2KBA would take on the data sets on which the
# packages are compared, if its time only grew in proportion to the number of
# locations (which it underestimates, as its time also grows with the number
# of tracks), from its time on the long tracks, which are the fewest; rounded
# down to the minute, as a lower bound
kba_compared <- 60 * floor(
  time_of("trip_split", "track2KBA", "long", kba_copies) *
    most_locations / kba_locations / 60
)
# how many times longer each operation takes on 10 times as many copies of
# the medium tracks, up to the most copies on which it was run; the speed
# filter of trip and track2KBA select the locations of each track from all
# the locations, so their times grow with the square of the number of tracks
medium_growth <- timings %>%
  filter(dataset == dataset_labels[["medium"]]) %>%
  group_by(operation, package) %>%
  summarise(
    growth = seconds[copies == max(copies)] /
      seconds[copies == max(copies) / 10],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    quadratic = package == "track2KBA" |
      (package == "trip" & operation == operation_labels[["speed_filter"]])
  )
# the text below assumes that the overhead of each track is less than a
# millisecond for the operations of tidytracks, that track2KBA was also run on
# 10 times fewer copies than the most on which it was run, and that, on the
# medium tracks, 10 times as many copies take the speed filter of trip and
# track2KBA more than 30 times as long, and the other operations less than 20
# times as long (about in proportion to the number of locations, give or take
# the variation of single timings)
stopifnot(
  all(vapply(
    names(operation_labels),
    function(operation) per_track_ms(operation, "tidytracks") < 1,
    logical(1)
  )),
  (kba_copies / 10) %in% all_copies,
  length(track_ratio) == 1,
  all(medium_growth$growth[medium_growth$quadratic] > 30),
  all(medium_growth$growth[!medium_growth$quadratic] < 20)
)
```

```{r summary_numbers, include = FALSE}
# the range of the times of the other packages relative to tidytracks, for
# the step distances on the data sets on which the packages are compared, and
# the slowest of them
distance_ratios <- fmt(range(vapply(
  c("move2", "amt", "trip"),
  function(package) {
    vapply(
      compared_sets,
      function(dataset) ratio("distance", package, dataset),
      numeric(1)
    )
  },
  numeric(length(compared_sets))
)))
slowest_distance <- compared %>%
  filter(operation == operation_labels[["distance"]]) %>%
  slice_max(seconds, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
# its package, as code in the text
slowest_package <- paste0("`", slowest_distance$package, "`")
```

```{r plot_functions, include = FALSE}
# one colour per package
package_colours <- c(
  tidytracks = "#2a78d6",
  move2 = "#8e5bd0",
  amt = "#eb6834",
  trip = "#1baf7a",
  track2KBA = "#c4373b"
)
# times on a log scale, labelled in seconds, minutes and hours, every factor
# of 10 (or of about 3, for the plot of the data sets on which the packages
# are compared)
time_labels <- c(
  "0.01" = "0.01 s", "0.03" = "0.03 s", "0.1" = "0.1 s", "0.3" = "0.3 s",
  "1" = "1 s", "3" = "3 s", "10" = "10 s", "60" = "1 min", "180" = "3 min",
  "600" = "10 min", "1800" = "30 min", "3600" = "1 h"
)
time_breaks <- as.numeric(names(time_labels))
# 0.01 s, 0.1 s, 1 s, 10 s, 1 min, 10 min and 1 h
decades <- c(1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12)
```

## Summary

- Given the same settings, the packages give the same results, except at
  the ends of some tracks and trips, and up to the differences between
  geodesic distances and distances on a sphere.
- `tidytracks` is the fastest for the three operations. On
  `r size_of("season", what = "total")` locations, in
  `r size_of("season")` tracks of
  `r size_of("season", what = "locations")` locations or
  `r size_of("year")` tracks of `r size_of("year", what = "locations")`
  locations, it computes the step distances in
  `r time_range("distance", "tidytracks")`, whereas the other packages
  take `r distance_ratios[1]` to `r distance_ratios[2]` times as long (up to
  `r fmt_time(slowest_distance$seconds)` with `r slowest_package`). Its speed
  filter runs the same algorithm as that of `trip`, which takes
  `r ratio_range("speed_filter", "trip")` times as long, and more on more
  tracks
  (`r secs("speed_filter", "trip", "medium")` for
  `r size_of("medium")` tracks of
  `r size_of("medium", what = "locations")` locations, against
  `r secs("speed_filter", "tidytracks", "medium")`). `track2KBA` takes
  `r ratio_range("trip_split", "track2KBA", growth_sets, kba_copies)` times
  as long to split the tracks into trips, on
  `r size_of("medium", kba_copies, "total")` locations
  (`r secs("trip_split", "track2KBA", "medium", kba_copies)` for
  `r size_of("medium", kba_copies)` tracks, against
  `r secs("trip_split", "tidytracks", "medium", kba_copies)` for
  `tidytracks`), and would take more than `r fmt_time(kba_compared)` on
  `r size_of("season", what = "total")` locations.
- The time of `tidytracks` grows in proportion to the number of locations,
  and hardly depends on the number of tracks: it handles all the tracks at
  once, and adds less than a millisecond per track, whereas `amt` adds
  `r per_track("distance", "amt")` ms per track to the step distances. The
  speed filter of `trip` and `track2KBA` select the locations of each track
  from all the locations, so their times grow with the square of the number
  of tracks.

The packages are run with the same settings on copies of four sets of
simulated tracks (see [The data sets](#the-data-sets) and
[Running the operations](#running-the-operations)). They are compared on
`r size_of("season", what = "total")` locations in long tracks: copies of
tracks of a season and of a year, i.e. `r size_of("season")` tracks of
`r size_of("season", what = "locations")` locations, and
`r size_of("year")` tracks of `r size_of("year", what = "locations")`
locations. To show how the times grow with the size of the data, the data
sets of medium tracks (of `r size_of("medium", what = "locations")`
locations) and of long tracks (of `r size_of("long", what = "locations")`
locations) grow from a single copy of the simulated tracks
(`r size_of("medium", 1)` and `r size_of("long", 1)` tracks) to
`r most_copies` copies (`r size_of("medium", what = "total")` locations).

## Do the packages give the same results?

```{r table_checks, echo = FALSE}
# the locations flagged differently by the speed filters
flagged <- count("speed_filter", "tidytracks", "locations flagged")
speed_filter_diff <- if (
  check_total("speed_filter", "trip", "locations flagged differently") == 0
) {
  paste0("none (of the ", flagged, " flagged locations)")
} else {
  paste0(
    count("speed_filter", "trip", "locations flagged differently"),
    " of the ", flagged, " flagged locations, in ",
    count_of(
      "speed_filter", "trip", "tracks with locations flagged differently",
      "track"
    )
  )
}
tibble::tribble(
  ~operation, ~package, ~difference,
  "Step distances", "move2",
  paste0(
    "up to ", signif(distance_diff("move2"), 2), "% (on a sphere)"
  ),
  "Step distances", "amt",
  paste0("up to ", signif(distance_diff("amt"), 2), "% (on a sphere)"),
  "Step distances", "trip", "none (up to rounding errors)",
  "Speed filter", "trip", speed_filter_diff,
  "Trip split", "track2KBA",
  paste0(
    "only at the ends of trips (",
    count_of(
      "trip_split", "track2KBA", "returns to the nest in a trip", "location"
    ),
    ") and of tracks (",
    count_of(
      "trip_split", "tidytracks", "trips of the last location of a track",
      "trip"
    ),
    ")"
  )
) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Operation", "Package", "Difference from tidytracks"),
    align = "lll",
    caption = paste(
      "Differences between the results, on the simulated medium and long",
      "tracks (their copies give the same results)."
    )
  )
```

- **Step distances**: `move2` and `amt` measure the steps on a sphere rather
  than on the ellipsoid (with `sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)`, they give the same
  distances as `tidytracks`).
- **Speed filter**: the two packages flag the same locations, except in
  tracks whose second-to-last location is an outlier
  (`r count_of("speed_filter", "trip", "tracks with locations flagged differently", "track")`
  here). `tidytracks` then flags the locations before the outlier, one at a
  time, until the speeds to the outlier are low enough, whereas `trip` (in
  version `r trip_version`) flags only the location just before it, as it
  computes the speeds between locations two steps apart wrongly for
  longitudes and latitudes. Neither package can flag the first two and last
  two locations of a track, whose speeds are not computed by the filter, and
  an outlier among them can make them flag other locations of the same track
  instead
  (`r count("speed_filter", "both", "outliers among the first two or last two locations of a track", zero = "none")`
  of the `r count("speed_filter", "both", "outliers")` simulated outliers are
  among them; `check_first_last = TRUE` makes `tidytracks` also check the
  first and last locations).
- **Trip split**: `track2KBA` includes in each trip the first location back
  within 5 km of the nest, and, when the last location of a track is the
  first one beyond 5 km of the nest, `tidytracks` makes it a trip of its own
  (an incomplete one), whereas `track2KBA` does not.

## How long do they take?

On `r size_of("season", what = "total")` locations in long tracks (copies of
the tracks of a season and of a year):

```{r plot_timings, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(compared, aes(x = seconds, y = package, colour = package)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  # the packages that were not run on these data sets
  geom_text(
    data = not_run,
    aes(x = sqrt(prod(range(compared$seconds))), label = "not run"),
    colour = "grey40",
    size = 3
  ) +
  # each operation with its own packages
  facet_grid(operation ~ data_set, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = time_breaks, labels = time_labels) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = package_colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Time (log scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(2, "lines"),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
    panel.border = element_rect(
      colour = "grey70",
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.5
    )
  )
```

```{r table_timings, echo = FALSE}
# one column per package; empty for the packages that do not have an
# operation
compared %>%
  bind_rows(not_run) %>%
  mutate(time = ifelse(is.na(seconds), "not run", fmt_time(seconds))) %>%
  select(data_set, operation, package, time) %>%
  arrange(data_set, operation, package) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = package, values_from = time, values_fill = "") %>%
  select(data_set, operation, any_of(package_levels)) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Data set", "Operation",
      intersect(package_levels, levels(droplevels(timings$package)))
    ),
    align = "llrrrrr",
    caption = paste(
      "Time of each operation on all the tracks of the data sets of",
      "copies of the tracks of a season and of a year."
    )
  )
```

- **Step distances**: `tidytracks` is the fastest: `move2` takes
  `r ratio_range("distance", "move2")` times as long, `amt`
  `r ratio_range("distance", "amt")` times and `trip`
  `r ratio_range("distance", "trip")` times. `tidytracks` computes the
  distances of all the tracks at once (with `geodist`), whereas `amt` and
  `trip` measure each track in turn.
- **Speed filter**: `tidytracks` and `trip` run the same algorithm, in R, but
  `trip` filters each track in turn (selecting its locations from all the
  locations), and computes the speeds between all the remaining locations
  again in each pass of the filter, whereas `tidytracks` filters all the
  tracks at once, only computes again the speeds around the locations removed
  in the previous pass, and only computes geodesic distances where the speeds
  could exceed the maximum (which it finds with a fast upper bound of the
  distances): `trip` takes `r ratio_range("speed_filter", "trip")` times as
  long. Its time also grows with the square of the number of tracks (see
  [How the times grow](#how-the-times-grow)): on the same number of
  locations in `r size_of("medium")` medium tracks, it takes
  `r secs("speed_filter", "trip", "medium")`, against
  `r secs("speed_filter", "tidytracks", "medium")` for `tidytracks`.
- **Trip split**: `track2KBA` was not run on these data sets, as it would
  take more than `r fmt_time(kba_compared)` on them
  (`r fmt(most_locations / kba_locations)` times its time on the
  `r size_of("long", kba_copies, "total")` locations of
  `r size_of("long", kba_copies)` long tracks, if its time only grew in
  proportion to the number of locations, whereas it also grows with the
  number of tracks). On `r kba_copies` copies of the medium and long tracks,
  it takes
  `r ratio_range("trip_split", "track2KBA", growth_sets, kba_copies)` times
  as long as `tidytracks`
  (`r secs("trip_split", "track2KBA", "medium", kba_copies)` on the
  `r size_of("medium", kba_copies)` medium tracks, and
  `r secs("trip_split", "track2KBA", "long", kba_copies)` on the
  `r size_of("long", kba_copies)` long tracks), as it goes through the
  locations of each track one at a time, in R (see below).

## How the times grow

```{r plot_growth, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(growth_timings, aes(x = total, y = seconds, colour = package)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_grid(dataset ~ operation) +
  scale_x_log10(
    labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())
  ) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = time_breaks[decades],
    labels = time_labels[decades]
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = package_colours) +
  labs(
    x = "Locations (log scale)",
    y = "Time (log scale)",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(1.5, "lines"),
    # room for the last label of the x axis
    plot.margin = margin(5.5, 15, 5.5, 5.5),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.border = element_rect(
      colour = "grey70",
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.5
    )
  )
```

The data sets grow by copying the tracks, from `r size_of("medium", 1)`
medium tracks or `r size_of("long", 1)` long tracks
(`r size_of("medium", 1, "total")` locations) to `r size_of("medium")`
medium tracks or `r size_of("long")` long tracks
(`r size_of("medium", what = "total")` locations). The times of `tidytracks`,
`move2` and `amt`, and the step distances of `trip`, grow about in proportion
to the number of locations: on the most copies of the medium tracks,
`tidytracks` takes about
`r per_location("distance", "tidytracks", "medium")` µs per location for the
step distances, `r per_location("speed_filter", "tidytracks", "medium")` µs
for the speed filter, and `r per_location("trip_split", "tidytracks", "medium")`
µs for the trips, against
`r per_location("distance", "move2", "medium")` µs for the step distances of
`move2`.

The medium and long tracks have the same number of locations, but the medium
tracks are `r track_ratio` times as many, so the difference between their
times gives the overhead of each track (e.g. to select its locations, or to
build its results). `tidytracks` and `move2` compute the step distances of
all the tracks at once, so their times hardly depend on the number of tracks
(`r secs("distance", "tidytracks", "medium")` with `tidytracks` for
`r size_of("medium")` tracks, against
`r secs("distance", "tidytracks", "long")` for `r size_of("long")` tracks),
whereas `amt` and `trip` add about `r per_track("distance", "amt")` ms and
`r per_track("distance", "trip")` ms per track. Likewise, the speed filter of
`tidytracks` runs on all the tracks at once
(`r secs("speed_filter", "tidytracks", "medium")` for `r size_of("medium")`
tracks, against `r secs("speed_filter", "tidytracks", "long")` for
`r size_of("long")` tracks).

The speed filter of `trip` and `track2KBA` select the locations of each track
from all the locations, which takes longer the more locations there are, so
the overhead of each track grows with the size of the data: `trip` adds about
`r per_track("speed_filter", "trip", most_copies / 10)` ms per track to the
speed filter on `r most_copies / 10` copies of the tracks, and
`r per_track("speed_filter", "trip")` ms on `r most_copies` copies. Their
times thus grow with the square of the number of tracks: ten times as many
copies of the medium tracks take `trip`
`r growth("speed_filter", "trip", "medium", most_copies / 10)` times as long
to filter them (from `r size_of("medium", most_copies / 10)` to
`r size_of("medium")` tracks), and `track2KBA`
`r growth("trip_split", "track2KBA", "medium", kba_copies / 10)` times as
long to split them into trips (from `r size_of("medium", kba_copies / 10)` to
`r size_of("medium", kba_copies)` tracks), as it also adds the trips of each
track to those of the previous tracks with `rbind()`, which copies them all
each time.

# How the benchmark was run

The benchmark takes about
`r round(as.numeric(session$value[session$item == "run time (minutes)"]) / 10) * 10`
minutes to run, so it was run once with the script
`vignettes/articles/code/operations_benchmark.R` (in the source code of the
package), and its results are read here from the directory
`vignettes/articles/data`. It uses tracks simulated beforehand with the
script `vignettes/articles/code/operations_benchmark_tracks.R`, and stored in
the same directory, so it can be run again (e.g. on another machine) without
simulating them. The code shown below is taken from these two scripts.
Timings depend on the machine (see
[Machine and software](#machine-and-software)), but the differences between
the packages, and how the times grow with the size of the data, should be
similar on other machines.

The benchmark uses these packages:

```{r packages, message = FALSE}
```

## Simulating tracks

The tracks are those of a central place forager, such as a seabird breeding
in a colony, with a GPS location every 5 minutes:

```{r simulate-tracks}
```

For example, the first two days of three tracks (the black points are the
nests, and the lines that leave the map go to outliers):

```{r example_tracks, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3}
example_tracks <- simulate_tracks(
  "example",
  n_tracks = 3,
  n_locations = 576,
  seed = 1
)
ggplot(example_tracks, aes(lon, lat)) +
  geom_path(colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(
    aes(nest_lon, nest_lat),
    data = distinct(example_tracks, id, nest_lon, nest_lat),
    colour = "black",
    size = 2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~id) +
  coord_quickmap(
    xlim = mean(example_tracks$nest_lon) + c(-1.4, 1.4),
    ylim = mean(example_tracks$nest_lat) + c(-0.8, 0.8)
  ) +
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## The data sets

We simulate four sets of tracks: tracks of medium length, and fewer, longer
tracks, with the same number of locations in all (about three and a half days
and five weeks of tracking respectively), and a few tracks of a season and of
a year (about three and a half months and a year of tracking):

```{r simulate-datasets, eval = FALSE}
```

The tracks were simulated once (with `code/operations_benchmark_tracks.R`),
and stored in `data/operations_benchmark_tracks.rds`, from which the
benchmark reads them:

```{r read-tracks, eval = FALSE}
```

The time taken by an operation on a set of tracks has two parts: one that
grows with the number of locations, and an overhead for each track. To see
how each part grows, the operations are timed on more and more copies of the
medium and long tracks. The packages are compared on copies of the tracks of
a season and of a year, with as many locations as the most copies of the
medium and long tracks:

```{r copies, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r table_data_sets, echo = FALSE}
# one row per number of locations, and one column per set of simulated
# tracks, with the number of tracks of its copies
timings %>%
  distinct(dataset, tracks, total) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = dataset, values_from = tracks) %>%
  arrange(total) %>%
  mutate(across(
    everything(),
    ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), "", formatC(.x, format = "d", big.mark = ","))
  )) %>%
  select(total, all_of(unname(dataset_labels))) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Locations",
      paste(
        "Tracks of",
        vapply(
          names(dataset_labels),
          function(dataset) size_of(dataset, what = "locations"),
          character(1)
        ),
        "locations"
      )
    ),
    align = "rrrrr",
    caption = paste(
      "The data sets: the number of tracks of each length (copies of the",
      "simulated tracks), for each number of locations."
    )
  )
```

## Running the operations

Each package works on its own class of objects: a `move2` object for
`tidytracks` and `move2`, a `track_xyt` for `amt`, a `trip` object (a
`SpatialPointsDataFrame` from `sp`) for `trip`, and data frames for
`track2KBA`. These are built from the data frame of locations of each data
set (outside of the timings):

```{r inputs, eval = FALSE}
```

The operations are then run with each package, on all the tracks of a data
set:

```{r operations, eval = FALSE}
```

The settings are matched so that the packages give the same results:

- **Step distances**: `tidytracks` and `trip` compute geodesic distances on
  the WGS84 ellipsoid (with the `geodist` package), whereas `move2` and `amt`
  use `sf::st_distance()`, which, with `s2` (the default of `sf`), computes
  great circle distances on a sphere. `tidytracks`, `move2` and `amt` give
  `NA` for the last location of each track, and `trip` gives 0. `amt` measures
  the steps of a single track, so its tracks are nested and measured in
  turn, as in its documentation, and this is included in its time.
- **Speed filter**: `tidytracks` and `trip` run the same algorithm, with a
  maximum speed of 120 km/h (`trip` takes it in km/h, for longitudes and
  latitudes). The optional check of the first and last locations of each
  track of `tidytracks` is off by default.
- **Trip split**: both packages use the nest of each animal, start a trip when
  the animal goes further than 5 km from it, end it when it comes back
  within 5 km, and keep the locations at the nest. `track2KBA` drops trips
  shorter than a minimum duration, which is set to 0 here, as `tidytracks`
  has none.

Each operation is run once, on an otherwise idle machine, and on a single
performance core of its CPU (see
[Running the benchmark again](#running-the-benchmark-again)); the operations
that take long are timed precisely enough by a single run:

```{r timing, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r run-benchmark, eval = FALSE}
```

The results of each package are then compared with those of `tidytracks`, on
the simulated medium and long tracks:

```{r checks, eval = FALSE}
```

## From the results to the tables and plots

The benchmark saves its results in `data/operations_benchmark_*.csv`, which
are read and summarised for the [results](#results) above with this code:

```{r, ref.label = c("results_packages", "read_results", "read_timings"), eval = FALSE}
```

and the plots of the timings are drawn with:

```{r, ref.label = c("plot_functions", "plot_timings", "plot_growth"), eval = FALSE}
```

## Running the benchmark again

To run the benchmark again (e.g. after changing `tidytracks`, or on another
machine), install `tidytracks` (with `R CMD INSTALL`, rather than loading it
with `devtools::load_all()`, which compiles its C++ code without
optimisation) and the other packages, and run, on an otherwise idle machine
with more than `r session$value[session$item == "peak memory (GB)"]` GB of
memory (the most that the benchmark used, on the largest data sets):

```sh
cd vignettes/articles
taskset -c 4 Rscript code/operations_benchmark.R
```

which overwrites `data/operations_benchmark_*.csv`; then render this article
again. `taskset -c 4` (on Linux) runs R on core 4 only: on a CPU with
performance and efficiency cores, such as the Intel i9-13900 used here, the
efficiency cores are almost half as fast, and R could otherwise move from one
kind of core to the other during the benchmark, which would change the times
of some operations more than others. Use one of the performance cores
(`lscpu -e` lists the cores, with their maximum frequency), or drop
`taskset -c 4` on a CPU whose cores are all the same.

`Rscript code/operations_benchmark.R quick` runs everything on the first
locations of a few tracks, to check the script, and saves its results in a
temporary directory instead. The simulated tracks are only needed again for a
different simulation: `Rscript code/operations_benchmark_tracks.R` simulates
them and overwrites `data/operations_benchmark_tracks.rds`.
